pr.title: Stall computing instance for drop shim until it has no unsubstituted const params
pr.description:
Do not inline the drop shim for types that still have unsubstituted const params.

## Why?

#127030 ICEs because it tries to inline the drop shim for a type with an unsubstituted const param. In order to generate this shim, this requires calling the drop shim builder, which invokes the trait solver to compute whether constituent types need drop (since we compute if a type is copy to disqualify any `Drop` behavior):

https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/9c3bc805dd9cb84019c124b9a50fdff1e62a7ec9/compiler/rustc_mir_dataflow/src/elaborate_drops.rs#L378

However, since we don't keep the param-env of the instance we resolved the item for, we use the wrong param-env:
https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/blob/9c3bc805dd9cb84019c124b9a50fdff1e62a7ec9/compiler/rustc_mir_transform/src/shim.rs#L278
(which is the param-env of `std::ptr::drop_in_place`)

This param-env is notably missing `ConstParamHasTy` predicates, and since we removed the type from consts in https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/125958, we literally cannot prove these predicates in this (relatively) empty param-env. This currently happens in places like the MIR inliner, but may happen elsewhere such as in lints that resolve terminators.

## What?

We force the inliner to not consider calls for `drop_in_place` for types that have unsubstituted const params.

## So what?

This may negatively affect MIR inlining, but I doubt this matters in practice, and fixes a beta regression, so let's fix it. I will look into approaches for fixing this in a more maintainable way, perhaps delaying the creation of drop shim bodies until codegen (like how intrinsics work).
pr.author: compiler-errors

analysis.originalLogic: In `check_mir_is_available` inside the MIR inliner, an `InstanceKind::DropGlue(_, Some(ty))` callee is treated as having MIR available regardless of whether `ty` still contains unsubstituted const parameters. This lets the inliner resolve/generate the drop shim immediately, which invokes the drop shim builder using the param-env of `std::ptr::drop_in_place` rather than the param-env of the resolved instance.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: The historically incorrect behavior is to inline (or attempt to resolve the MIR for) a `drop_in_place` / drop-glue shim for a type that still has unsubstituted const params, e.g. a type involving a generic const `M`. Generating that shim invokes the trait solver under the wrong, relatively empty param-env, which lacks `ConstParamHasTy` predicates, so the predicates cannot be proven and compilation ICEs. The fix is not a different code rewrite of the callee: it stalls availability by returning `Err("still needs substitution")` for `DropGlue` instances whose type has `TypeFlags::HAS_CT_PARAM`, so the inliner does not process them until the const params are substituted.
analysis.inputDomain: MIR inlining (`-Zinline-mir=yes`) of a call to `std::ptr::drop_in_place` on a type that has a generic const parameter and contains a type with `Drop`, reachable from an `#[inline]` generic function. The const parameter may either remain unsubstituted (the stalling case) or be concretely substituted (the inlinable case).
analysis.summary: Bug fix in the MIR inliner: do not resolve/inline the drop shim for a `DropGlue` instance whose type still has unsubstituted const params. Such shim construction uses the wrong param-env and cannot prove `ConstParamHasTy`, causing an ICE; the inliner now stalls until substitution.
analysis.trigger: The inliner considers `InstanceKind::DropGlue(_, Some(ty))` where `ty.has_type_flags(TypeFlags::HAS_CT_PARAM)` is true, typically a `drop_in_place` call on `Foo<Dorp, M>` inside a generic function parameterized by const `M`.
preconditions: MIR inlining is enabled, e.g. via `-Zinline-mir=yes`.
The callee is a `DropGlue` instance with a concrete type recorded (`Some(ty)`).
The dropped type still contains an unsubstituted const parameter (`HAS_CT_PARAM`).
The type contains a constituent needing drop, so building the shim queries the trait solver for `Copy`/drop behavior.
The shim builder is invoked with the param-env of `std::ptr::drop_in_place`, which lacks the original instance's `ConstParamHasTy` predicates.
pitfalls: This is a workaround that reduces MIR inlining for such drop shims, not a repair of the drop shim builder's param-env; the PR leaves a FIXME (#127030) and mentions a possible future redesign delaying drop shim bodies until codegen.
The stall applies only to `DropGlue` with `Some(ty)` and `HAS_CT_PARAM`; it must not be generalized to all drop glue or all const-generic instances.
The issue is about unsubstituted const params, not ordinary generic type parameters or borrowing/copy semantics; do not conflate those conditions.
No compiler execution or ICE reproduction is claimed here; the diagnosis is source- and PR-description-based.
analysis.testStrategy: Add a UI build-pass regression test with `//@ compile-flags: -Zinline-mir=yes --crate-type=lib` containing a const-generic `Foo<T, const N: usize>([T; N])`, a `Dorp` type implementing `Drop`, and an `#[inline] pub unsafe fn drop<const M: usize>(x: *mut Foo<Dorp, M>)` that calls `std::ptr::drop_in_place(x)`. For a two-program differential setup, keep the source identical except for the transformation-relevant const parameter: one program leaves `M` unsubstituted in the inline function (must stall rather than ICE); the other fixes it to a concrete value so the drop shim can be inlined. The historical regression test is the parameterized `drop<const M: usize>` variant and asserts successful compilation.
